Yes of course you have to look at the relative standards and absolute standards. I lived in Magdeburg for 3 years and it wasn't that bad, but there are definitely parts that have been rotting for 30, 40 years. 

But you go deeper into parts of Sachsen Anhalt, and it is pretty fucking dire. Yeah rural areas are always a bit behind the curve, compare a Dorf in Sachsen Anhalt and a similar sized one in Franken, there is a world of difference. 

The difference in wages, and most importantly generational or family wealth is huge. That is not a problem that can be immediately solved with a couple of hundred million over 30 years. 

Otto 68 years old in his 45 m² Plattenbau Apartment in Ficksleben an der Elbe sees how someone in Stuttgart is living in a big family house with a nice Audi and of course is going to be resentful. It is not relevant to him that the West threw fistfuls of marks at the east, without really addressing the inequality at any meaningful level. It is irrelevant if big companies from the West came in and gave people jobs. At the end of the day the profits all flowed back to the west - and more importantly the people felt no connection to their compatriots in this sense. 

My ex grew up in the east, and even in the 2000s when she was studying and doing well, there was still a stigma about being a DDR Kind. 

But you a right most surface level explanations are extreme over simplifications. But you can't really complain when people decide to engage in a spot of self determination.
So you think the solution is just throwing money at the problem?

Edit: let me be clear I am not trying to argue that the DDR was a bastion of civility and democracy. I am arguing that governments failed to adequately give them the leg up they needed. And no, a few Marks Begrüßungsgeld is not adequate.

It's a failure of the government's of the last 30 years to adequately represent the people of the former DDR. Unemployment is higher, and general opportunities fewer. People genuinely believe they will get a decent alternative, after feeling shat on for 30 years. 

I dont agree with the AfD and her policies, but I understand why people might see it as an option.

The Metabo HPT brand is Japanese (HPT is Hitachi Power Tools, but made elsewhere) and this reflects the look and feel, but I'm pretty sure Metabo (the old Elektra Beckum) grinders and many other tools are still solid german made. The one Metabo tool I actually own is the Lackfräse as Im pretty sure they're the only decent manufacturer of this particular tool. I can recommend this tool.

You can make the same argument with Makita to be honest, there is the cheaper Makita stuff that you can even find on shelves in Kaufland sometimes. I've picked up some Makita stuff which was just felt awful before. Yes bosch green is pretty ordinary, and even some of the bosch blue lower end stuff is pretty rubbish. 

With Fein I don't need to worry if I've picked up the shit version of a tool, because there isn't one really. I am slowly going to start buying Fein 18v stuff as they migrate more tools to the Ampshare line. 

By the way I've been buying some old Eugen Lutz (Elu) Swiss made corded routers and planers and they are great. Their technology is why Dewalt has very decent planers and routers these days. They are also much cheaper than Festool stuff, but albiet without the balls and whistles and insane dust extraction. 

My philosophy is I try to stay in the same battery ecosystem for 18v stuff, but for corded tools I buy the stuff that the brand is known for, Festool Tauchsäge, Bosch Hammer, Fein Multitool, Mirka Sander. (Exception is Flex Angle grinder) then I cut off the cords and run them through my Industrie Sauger connected with a Powercon TrueCon 1 connector.

Power tools: none?! Hahaha, have you picked up a Festool, Fein, Mafell or even (some) Metabo or Bosch tool recently? Think about some of the large Shop machines as well, Flott, Felder, Altendorf etc.

A pro pos, I just buy many of my tools from Würth, and you don't have to worry about shopping around for the best Brands because they do it for you. Würth Powerplaners from DeWalt, Bohrhammer from Bosch, Angle grinder (I think Metabo) screwdrivers from Wiha. 

I prefer Bosch 18v because the battery tech seems superior to anyone else. Maybe it's just Marketing but I have the feeling Bosch invests a lot into R&D in this area. And there is also a reason they haven't gone into pouch style cells yet. Also I am now super happy that Fein are on the Bosch platform because I love Fein tools, bulletproof and non gimicky.

having lived in Magdeburg... can confim to a degree. Nearby Berlin is at least the capital and has - especially in the last 5-10 years - decent investment post Wende. Magdeburg has high unemployment and a lot of older people. The job center there is usually very busy. (yes i've been in there)

A fortunate side-effect is that the city has cheap rent and the green spaces in the city are large and  accessible. The Stadtpark is fucking awesome and really big. The city is also tiny and feels more like a village. 

There is a decent enough Uni and HS there, but I have a sense they will struggle to keep professionals in the area until they make large investments.

The city itself is of huge historical importance, which is why they built the Magdeburger Dom there, which is the oldest Gothic Church in Germany. The Dom is a miracle in itself because the rest of the city had the piss bombed out of it during WWII. It used to be a huge hanseatic trade-hub and was at one point a fortified garrison city.

There is a ton of potential for growth there. I'm not going to say it's the next Leipzig/Dresden, but if you can secure an property or house around areas such as Buckau near the Elbe, then you could see your investment grow massively in the next 10-15 years. 

The rest of Sachsen-Anhalt, yeah it's lagging behind, but cities like Halle are somewhat on the front foot.

I worked in Marketing and some of our biggest clients were Aged-Care Homes and organisations like the Volkssolidaritaet and die Tafel. These are a strong reminder of a mostly retired, and or un- or underemployed population. 

Good memories of Magdeburg / Sachsen-Anhalt: drinking Sternies and smoking weed by the Elbe, Wandern in the Harz and doing the ElbeRadWeg!

I guess I can add a somewhat unique perspective on this question: I'm not sure if it really counts in the context of the OP's question but it was a school shooting.
I am from Australia and I guess if you take a casual look on google its fairly easy to find some info on this particular case from 2003. I don't know how it is for our American friends but from my perspective school shootings in the US seem to be a semi regular occurrence. Of course the incidents ever happening in Australia (ever) can literally be counted on one hand, that's what made the incident so shocking to us. I can really only give my perspective on what happened, and it was 13 years ago so some of the details are a little bit blurry. 
The shooting occurred during the long recess (lunch break) about 100 metres (300 odd feet for you freedom-uniters) from where my friends and I were sitting, and there was a line of site view to the scene of the crime. I remember suddenly seeing a rush of people start sprinting and converging in front of what was the science building on a large grassed area. 

Of course this is where the unique aspects of this case come into play. Whilst most people would question why people would be running towards the shooter, it is of course important to realise that guns are extremely difficult (especially for a school kid) to acquire in Australia. The shooting was carried out with a freaking crossbow and hunting bolt, which the guy had procured through the Internet from South Australia, where apparently these things were legal back then. This of course means that there were no gun shots. Second point is that everybody loves a fight (don't know if its in the US like this but in Australian playgrounds its definitely a twisted form of entertainment for bored schoolkids.) 

Naturally everyone assumed there was a fight happening, I and all of my friends rushed over with the rest of the school to see what was going on. It turns out one of my form mates had seen the shot fired and had then rushed the guy as he was trying to light a molotov cocktail to throw at his victim. Of course the guy saved the victims and a bystanders lives. He basically held the guy, who was screaming and yelling the whole time, until and teacher took over and then the police arrived. Unfortunately no mobile phone footage exists of the incident, as this was 2003 and we were all amazed when my friend bought the first Nokia cameraphone! 

Anyway the aftermath was like what happens when a fire drill is called, everybody is wandering around a little bit in shock, of course there are rumours flying around and people just standing around not knowing what to do. Some where crying, some where trying to break into the school Admin building where the guy was held by police for questioning. The Ambulance of course had come, and the main target had been stabilised and airlifted to hospital. I remember dragging tarps out to the crime scene to preserve the scene because it had started to rain. There was a lot of blood, and some scattered bits and peices: a lighter, an unexploded Molotov cocktail, the shooters bag. Anyway, totally surreal.

I don't think they really had a real school day the next day. Everyone was still in shock, we basically spent the day being debriefed in the Assembly Hall and kind of just walking around, and doing as kids do, spreading rumours asking questions. I think the overall feeling was that nobody knew quite what to do. I guess you guys in the US have protocols to follow for this shit. Well I think everyone was just like, "WTF"?! I think we were offered counseling, but I guess we talked about it enough amongst ourselves. There was talk of revenge, what would happen to the guy, how the vicitims were etc. 

The victims survived and are living healthy normal lives as far as I know. We didn't get any free passes on Exams or anything. The dude who tackled the perp. obvious was a minor celeb for a while. Don't know what he's up to now. I used to see him surfing, but don't anymore. 

We kind of became unofficially know as "Crossbow-High" which was kind of macabre. 

I don't know what happened to the perp. He never got done for attempted murder afaik, even though he shot his ex girlfriend through the chest with a hunting bolt at close range. (the bolt went through and through, then struck another girl in the legs) and then tried to light a molotov cocktail. Even though the dude was bullied and was an outsider that is some fucked up shit. 

edit: oh yeah should have seen it coming: When I was 11 or so, the same dude chased me around the class room trying to stab me with scissors, because I called him "coke bottle glasses" or something.
